body:
## Problem

`SSH.Software.compare_version` compares version strings with `<`/`>` (`if self.version < oversion`). String ordering treats `0.10.4` as lower than `0.7.2` and `10.0` as lower than `7.3`. `get_alg_timeframe` (line 1494/1496) and `output_compatibility` (line 1722) have the same flaw.

## Evidence

Reproduced on Python 3.14.7:
- `Software(libssh-0.10.4).compare_version('0.7.2')` → `-1`
- `Software(libssh-0.10.4).between_versions('0.1', '0.7.2')` → `True`, so CVE-2016-0739 is reported against libssh 0.10.4
- `Software(OpenSSH_10.0).compare_version('7.3')` → `-1`

Quoted line 805: `if self.version < oversion:`

## Impact

This is a security audit tool. For current libssh (0.10.x/0.11.x) it reports CVEs the server does not have. For OpenSSH 10.x it treats the server as older than 7.3, which skews the recommendations section: `get_alg_recommendations` skips algorithms "not available yet". Operators act on false output.

## Fix

Compare the numeric components as integer tuples, e.g. `tuple(int(x) for x in v.split('.'))`, in `compare_version`, and route `get_alg_timeframe`/`output_compatibility` through the same key function. Add test cases for `0.10.4 > 0.7.2` and `10.0 > 9.9`.

## Resolution
Added version_key() (integer tuple of numeric components), used in Software.compare_version, get_alg_timeframe and output_compatibility. Regression tests: test_version_compare.test_multi_digit_components_compare_numerically, test_timeframe (2 tests), test_ssh2.test_security_section_empty_for_libssh_0_10 (mutation-checked: fails when string comparison is restored).
title: Version comparison is lexicographic; multi-digit components misorder (false CVEs, wrong recommendations)

body:
## Problem

The getopt long option list declares `'port'` without a trailing `=`, so `--port` takes no argument. README and `usage()` both document `-p, --port=<port>`.

## Evidence

`lopts = ['help', 'ssh1', 'ssh2', 'ipv4', 'ipv6', 'port', ...]` (line 137-138).
Reproduced: `from_cmdline(['--port=2222','localhost'])` → usage + exit (GetoptError "option --port must not have an argument"); `['--port','2222','localhost']` also exits (2222 is taken as the host). `--level=warn` works because it is declared `'level='`.

## Impact

A documented CLI flag of the public interface fails every time. Scripts that use the long form cannot run.

## Fix

Change `'port'` to `'port='`. Add `--port=2222 localhost` and `--port 2222 localhost` cases to the cmdline test.

## Resolution
Long option declared as 'port='. test_auditconf covers --port=2222, --port 2222 and --port=abc.
title: Documented --port=<port> long option is unusable

body:
## Problem

`SSH.Socket.read_packet` trusts the server-supplied `packet_length` (`# XXX: validate length`). A packet whose payload length computes to 0 reaches `ord(payload[0:1])` on empty bytes. A huge length makes `ensure_read` buffer without bound for as long as the server keeps sending. The SSH2 `payload_length = packet_length - padding_length - 1` can go negative, and `read(negative)` reads the whole buffer.

## Evidence

Reproduced: banner `SSH-2.0-x`, then packet `struct.pack('>IB', 4, 3) + b'\x00'*3` → `TypeError: ord() expected a character, but string of length 0 found` (uncaught, stack trace, exit code 1 with no audit output).
Quoted line 1219: `# XXX: validate length`; line 1245: `packet_type = ord(payload[0:1])`.

## Impact

The tool's input is by definition an untrusted remote server. A hostile or broken server can crash the audit or make it consume unbounded memory. Either way the operator gets no result.

## Fix

Validate before reading. SSH2: reject when `padding_length < 4`, `payload_length < 1`, or `packet_length > 35000` (RFC 4253 §6.1 packet limit). SSH1: require `5 <= packet_length <= 262144`. Return `(-1, b'invalid packet length')` so `audit()` reports it through the normal error path. Add tests for zero payload, negative payload and oversize length.

## Resolution
read_packet rejects packet_length above MAX_PACKET_LENGTH (drains at most that many bytes and reports them, preserving the plaintext 'Protocol major versions differ.' fallback), SSH2 padding < 4 or empty payload, SSH1 length < 5. audit() reports struct.error from truncated KEXINIT/PUBLIC_KEY bodies as 'malformed ... packet'. Tests in test_hostile_server.py (empty payload, short padding, oversized length bounded read, truncated KEXINIT).
title: Malformed server packets crash the auditor with a traceback; packet length is never validated

body:
## Problem

`get_banner` calls `read_line()` on whatever bytes are buffered, including an unterminated fragment. A partial line such as `SSH-2.0-Open` matches `RX_BANNER` and becomes the banner. The rest of the line is then read as the first binary packet.

## Evidence

Reproduced with recv chunks `b'SSH-2.0-Open'`, `b'SSH_7.3\r\n'`: output is `[exception] invalid ssh packet (block size)`. The banner was parsed as software `Open`.
Loop: `while self.__banner is None and self.unread_len > 0: line = self.read_line()` (lines 1159-1160).

## Impact

Slow links, small MTUs and servers that write byte-by-byte can make the audit fail spuriously or misidentify the software.

## Fix

Only consume a line when the buffered data contains `\n`. Otherwise `recv()` more (with an overall line-length cap of 255 bytes per RFC 4253 §4.2) before parsing.

## Resolution
get_banner only parses complete lines (or a partial line at EOF / at MAX_LINE_LENGTH). test_hostile_server.test_banner_split_across_segments.
title: Banner split across TCP segments is parsed from a partial line

body:
## Problem

Pre-banner header lines, the banner and every KEXINIT algorithm name go to stdout unsanitised. `Utils.to_ascii` keeps ASCII control characters, including ESC (0x1b) and BEL.

## Evidence

Reproduced: header `\x1b[2J\x1b]0;pwned\x07hello` and banner `SSH-2.0-OpenSSH_7.3\x1b[1A` are emitted verbatim: `'(gen) header: \x1b[2J\x1b]0;pwned\x07hello\n(gen) banner: SSH-2.0-OpenSSH_7.3\x1b[1A...'`.
Sinks: `out.info('(gen) header: ' + '\n'.join(header))` (line 1824), `out.good('(gen) banner: {0}'.format(banner))` (line 1826), `output_algorithm` (line 1698).

## Impact

The audited server controls the auditor's terminal. It can clear the screen, move the cursor up to overwrite `[fail]` lines, or set the window title, and so make a weak server look clean. That defeats the tool's purpose.

## Fix

Before output, replace every non-printable character in server-derived strings (`c < ' ' or c == '\x7f'`, plus C1 0x80-0x9f) with `\xNN` via one helper applied in `SSH.Banner.parse`, header collection and `read_list`. Add a test asserting no `\x1b` from server data reaches stdout.

## Resolution
Output.escape() renders Cc/Zl/Zp characters (except newline and tab) as \xNN / \uNNNN at the single print choke point (plain, colorized and error output). Tests: test_server_control_characters_are_escaped, test_colors_still_applied_around_escaped_text, test_error_goes_to_stderr_at_any_level.
title: Server-controlled terminal escape sequences are printed raw (audit output spoofing)

body:
## Problem

`get_banner` loops `while self.__banner is None`, appending every non-banner line to `self.__header` with no line-count, byte or wall-clock limit. Only `recv` returning <0 ends it.

## Evidence

Reproduced: a socket returning `b'x'*100 + b'\r\n'` on every recv kept the loop running for 20000 recv calls. It stopped only when the stub raised; `header lines kept 20000`. Each recv is subject only to the 5 s per-read timeout, which a trickling server never trips.

## Impact

A tarpit or hostile server hangs the audit indefinitely while memory grows. Batch runs over many hosts stall on one bad target.

## Fix

Cap pre-banner data (e.g. 50 lines or 8192 bytes, and an overall deadline such as 10 s via `time.monotonic()`), then return `banner=None` so `audit()` reports "did not receive banner". Add a test with an endless header stream.

## Resolution
Pre-banner reading capped at MAX_PRE_BANNER_LINES=1024 (OpenSSH client limit) and BANNER_TIMEOUT=15s via time.monotonic(). Tests: test_endless_pre_banner_lines_stop, test_slow_pre_banner_lines_hit_deadline.
title: get_banner accumulates pre-banner lines without bound and never terminates

body:
## Problem

`_close_socket` calls `s.shutdown(socket.SHUT_RDWR)` then `s.close()` inside one bare `try/except: pass`. `shutdown` raises `OSError(ENOTCONN)` on a socket that never connected, which is exactly the `connect()` failure path, so `close()` never runs and the error is swallowed.

## Evidence

Reproduced: `_close_socket(socket.socket())` on an unconnected socket leaves `s.fileno() != -1` (still open). Called from `connect()` on every failed address (line 1134). `audit()` also recurses into `audit(aconf, 1)` (line 1986) without closing the SSH2 socket, relying on `__del__`.

## Impact

Each failed address family leaks a descriptor until garbage collection and emits a ResourceWarning. In long batch runs over many unreachable hosts the leaks accumulate.

## Fix

Put `close()` in a `finally`: `try: s.shutdown(socket.SHUT_RDWR) except OSError: pass; finally: s.close()`. In `audit()` use `with SSH.Socket(...) as s:` so the socket closes before the SSH1 fallback.

## Resolution
_close_socket closes in finally after a tolerated shutdown OSError; audit() uses `with SSH.Socket(...)` so the socket closes before the SSH1 fallback and on every sys.exit path; __del__ removed. Tests: test_errors.test_failed_connect_closes_socket, test_ssh2_server_simple asserts vsocket.closed.
title: _close_socket skips close() when shutdown() raises (fd leak on failed connect)

body:
## Problem

Every `[exception]` message goes through `out.fail` → `print()` to stdout before `sys.exit(1)`. Nothing is written to stderr.

## Evidence

Reproduced: connection reset before banner → stdout contains `'[exception] did not receive banner.\n'`. Sites: lines 1117, 1140, 1234, 1249, 2001.

## Impact

`ssh-audit.py host > report.txt` writes the failure into the report and shows nothing on the terminal. Batch consumers parsing stdout ingest error text as audit lines.

## Fix

Print `[exception]` messages with `file=sys.stderr` (e.g. an `Output.error` method that writes to stderr regardless of level) and keep the exit code 1. Update the error tests to capture stderr.

## Resolution
New Output.error() prints to stderr regardless of minlevel; all [exception] messages and usage errors use it. test_errors asserts exactly one stderr line per failure.
title: Errors are written to stdout, not stderr

body:
## Problem

`AuditConf.__setattr__` only stores names on an allow-list; any other name falls through with `valid=False` and is dropped without error.

## Evidence

Reproduced: `c = AuditConf(); c.colours = False` → no exception, `hasattr(c, 'colours')` is False, and colors stay enabled. Line 127: `if valid: object.__setattr__(self, name, value)` with no else.

## Impact

A misspelled option in calling code or a test is a silent no-op, so the configured behaviour differs from the written intent and nothing reports it.

## Fix

Raise `AttributeError(f'unknown option: {name}')` for unrecognised names. The ipv4/ipv6 branch sets `valid=False` deliberately (it writes `ipvo`); give it an explicit `return` instead of relying on the fall-through.

## Resolution
AuditConf.__setattr__ raises AttributeError for unknown names and ValueError for a non-sequence ipvo. test_audit_conf_rejects_unknown_attributes.
title: AuditConf silently discards unknown attribute assignments

body:
## Problem

Several definitions are never reached from `audit()`: `KexDH`, `KexGroup1` and `KexGroup14` (the start of SSH2 host-key fingerprinting, never called); `SSH.Protocol.MSG_NEWKEYS` and `MSG_KEXDH_REPLY`; `Fingerprint.md5`, because `output_fingerprint` is always called with `sha256=True`. Also `output_security_sub` computes `is_client`/`is_local` and never reads them, and line 1197 `self.__sock.send(data)` follows `return` statements in both branches and cannot run.

## Evidence

Reference counts in ssh-audit.py: `KexGroup1(` 1 (definition only), `KexGroup14(` 1, `send_init` 1, `MSG_NEWKEYS` 1, `MSG_KEXDH_REPLY` 1. `output_fingerprint(kex, pkm, True, maxlen)` (line 1883) is the only call. `fps` is populated only for SSH1 (line 1771), so SSH2 fingerprints are an unfinished feature.

## Impact

About 60 lines of dead code look like working features. bandit flags B324 (MD5) on the unreachable `md5` property, and readers can assume SSH2 fingerprints exist.

## Fix

Remove `KexDH`, `KexGroup1`, `KexGroup14`, the two unused constants, `Fingerprint.md5` with the `sha256` parameter, the unused locals and line 1197. Wiring SSH2 fingerprints is a feature and needs its own request.

## Resolution
Removed KexDH, KexGroup1, KexGroup14, MSG_NEWKEYS/MSG_KEXDH_INIT/MSG_KEXDH_REPLY, Fingerprint.md5 and output_fingerprint's kex/sha256 parameters, unused locals, and the unreachable send. output_fingerprint docstring states SSH2 fingerprints are not implemented. bandit B324 no longer reported.
title: Unwired code: KexDH/KexGroup1/KexGroup14, Fingerprint.md5, unused protocol constants and dead branches

body:
## Problem

The module carries Python 2.6/2.7 shims that no supported interpreter runs: `from __future__ import print_function`, the `text_type`/`binary_type`/`StringIO` switch, `Utils.to_ntext`/`to_utext`/`to_bytes`, the `_bitlength` fallback for ints without `bit_length`, `bytes(bytearray(v, 'utf-8'))`, `super(Cls, self)`, `object` base classes, `# type:` comments, `u''` literals, and a hand-rolled CRC32 table.

## Evidence

Line 31 `if sys.version_info >= (3,):  # pragma: nocover` with a py2 else-branch. Line 1915: `elif isinstance(v, text_type)` is unreachable on py3 because `text_type is str` and line 1913 already matched `str`. SSH1 CRC32 equals `binascii.crc32(data, 0xffffffff) ^ 0xffffffff` (verified: both give 0xb9c60808 for the fox string). test_buffer.py `test_bitlen` tests the Py2.6 fallback.

## Impact

Python 2 is EOL since 2020. The shims double the code paths that readers must reason about, block modern typing (annotations, dataclasses), and hide real type errors behind `Any`.

## Fix

Target Python 3.14 only. Delete the compat branch and `Utils` text helpers (use `str`/`bytes` directly), use `int.bit_length()`, replace the CRC table with the `binascii` expression, convert type comments to annotations, drop `object`/`super(...)` arguments, and remove `test_bitlen`'s py2.6 case.

## Resolution
Python 3.14 only: removed __future__, text_type/binary_type/StringIO switch, Utils class (unique_seq/parse_int now module functions), _bitlength fallback, bytearray conversions, object bases, super() args, type comments (converted to annotations). CRC32 table replaced with binascii (equivalence checked on 2000 random inputs). Tabs converted to spaces. Golden full-output dump byte-identical across every step.
title: Python 2 compatibility layer is dead weight on any supported interpreter

body:
## Problem

The type comments are unverified and wrong in places. `Dict` is used in type comments (lines 455, 1066, 1454, 1468) but never imported. Several functions declared to return a concrete type return `None`: `Banner.parse -> SSH.Banner`, `Software.parse -> SSH.Software`, `_extract_os_version -> str`, `get_alg_since_text -> text_type`. `test/mypy.ini` uses `silent_imports`, an option removed from mypy years ago, and nothing in CI runs a type check.

## Evidence

Import line 42-43: `from typing import List, Set, Sequence, Tuple, Iterable` / `Callable, Optional, Union, Any` (no `Dict`). Line 1012 `return None` under `# type: (text_type) -> SSH.Banner`. `.travis.yml` script runs only `py.test`.

## Impact

The types document a contract the code does not keep. Callers such as `output_security` rely on `None` returns the annotations deny, and no gate catches drift.

## Fix

When converting to inline annotations, declare `-> Banner | None` etc. Delete the stale `test/mypy.ini` and `mypy-py2.sh`/`mypy-py3.sh`. A stdlib-only toolchain has no type checker; document that typing is advisory (or allow a non-stdlib checker as a dev tool if wanted).

## Resolution
Inline annotations corrected (Optional returns, AlgorithmDB alias, NoReturn usage callback). mypy --strict gated as a prek hook (runs in CI lint job) and passes; pyright also reports 0 errors. Stale test/mypy.ini and mypy scripts deleted.
title: Declared types contradict the implementation and are never checked

body:
## Problem

The only pipeline definition is `.travis.yml` for travis-ci.org, which shut down in 2021, and the fork (origin github.com/ivuorinen/ssh-audit) has no `.github/workflows`. The matrix lists Python 2.6-3.5/pypy, all EOL. Installs are unpinned (`pip install --upgrade pytest pytest-cov coveralls`), and `after_success: coveralls` uploads to a service the fork is not registered with.

## Evidence

.travis.yml lines 1-17. `ls .github` → absent. README badges point to `api.travis-ci.org/arthepsy/ssh-audit.svg` and coveralls for the upstream repo.

## Impact

No commit or PR to this fork is tested or linted, so every defect in this audit could land or regress unobserved.

## Fix

Delete `.travis.yml`. Add `.github/workflows/ci.yml` on pull_request/push to master: `permissions: contents: read`, `actions/checkout` and `actions/setup-python` pinned to full commit SHAs with `persist-credentials: false`, Python 3.14, running `python -m unittest` and the lint step. Run `prek` with the same hooks. Replace the dead badges.

## Resolution
.travis.yml deleted. .github/workflows/ci.yml: push to master + pull_request, permissions contents: read, actions pinned to commit SHAs with persist-credentials: false, lint job via j178/prek-action, unittest on ubuntu/macos/windows with Python 3.14. actionlint and zizmor clean locally; not yet run on GitHub (branch not pushed).
title: CI targets defunct travis-ci.org with EOL Pythons; no pipeline gates this repository

body:
## Problem

Every test module imports `pytest` and uses fixtures/`pytest.raises`, so the suite cannot run under the stdlib. None of the confirmed defects is covered: long-option `--port=`, multi-digit version ordering, malformed/zero-length packets, fragmented banners, endless headers and escape sequences. `test_ssh2_server_simple` asserts only `len(lines) == 72` and `test_ssh1_server_simple` only `len(lines) == 10`. That validates line count, not content, so recommendations, compatibility and security output are effectively unchecked. `get_alg_recommendations` has no direct test. The `virtual_socket` fixture patches `socket.socket` but `_resolve` calls the real `socket.getaddrinfo('localhost', 22)`, coupling tests to host DNS.

## Evidence

`python3.14 -c 'import pytest'` → not installed; `command -v pytest` → not available. test_ssh2.py:142 `assert len(lines) == 72`. conftest.py patches only `create_connection` and `socket`.

## Impact

The suite cannot run in the target stdlib-only environment, and where it can run it passes against output that is wrong (false CVEs for libssh 0.10.x would not change the line count for a 7.3 banner).

## Fix

Port to `unittest` (`python -m unittest discover -s test`), with `contextlib.redirect_stdout` in place of `_OutputSpy` and `unittest.mock.patch` for `socket.socket`/`socket.getaddrinfo`. Replace the line-count asserts with assertions on specific lines (banner, a `[fail]` recommendation, the compatibility string). Add regression tests for each confirmed defect.

## Resolution
Suite ported to stdlib unittest (95 tests, `python -m unittest discover -s test`, passes with -W error). getaddrinfo mocked (no DNS coupling). SSH1/SSH2 simple tests assert concrete output lines; security section tested end to end; regression tests added for every fixed defect.
title: Test suite requires pytest and leaves the defective paths untested

body:
## Problem

README line 15 claims "compatible with Python 2.6+, Python 3.x and PyPy". The usage block omits `-h, --help`, which `usage()` prints. The badges point at defunct travis-ci.org and upstream coveralls. `usage()` hard-codes the upstream author contact `<email>` in the header of this fork's output. There are no instructions for running tests or lint.

## Evidence

README.md:2-3, 15, 18-31; ssh-audit.py:57 `uout.head('# {0} {1}, <email>\n'...)`; ssh-audit.py:61 `-h,  --help`.

## Impact

Users on this fork get wrong platform claims and are routed to the upstream author for fork issues. Contributors have no documented way to run the checks.

## Fix

State the Python 3.14 requirement, add `-h, --help` to usage, replace the badges with the GitHub Actions badge for ivuorinen/ssh-audit, add a Development section (`python -m unittest`, `prek run --all-files`), and make the usage header name the project URL instead of a personal mailbox.

## Resolution
README: Python 3.14 requirement, -h in usage, GitHub Actions badge, stale-DB caveat, stderr/NO_COLOR notes, Development section, Unreleased changelog. usage() header points to the project URL instead of the upstream mailbox.
title: README contradicts the code and the fork (Python 2.6+, missing -h, dead badges, upstream contact)

## Problem

LICENSE and the ssh-audit.py docstring both carry only `Copyright (C) 2016 Andris Raugulis`. The fork maintainer's copyright for new modifications is absent, and the full MIT text is duplicated in the source file, where the two copies can drift.

## Evidence

LICENSE:3; ssh-audit.py:4-24.

## Impact

Modifications made in this fork carry no ownership notice. The duplicated license text must be edited in two places.

Keep the original line (MIT requires it) and add `Copyright (C) 2026 Ismo Vuorinen` to LICENSE. Replace the docstring license body with an SPDX header (`# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT`) plus both copyright lines, and declare `license = "MIT"` / `license-files = ["LICENSE"]` in pyproject.toml.

LICENSE adds 'Copyright (C) 2026 Ismo Vuorinen' under the original notice; ssh-audit.py header is SPDX MIT with both copyright lines; pyproject declares license = "MIT", license-files = ["LICENSE"].
title: License notice names only the upstream author; fork copyright missing and header duplicated

body:
## Problem

ssh-audit.py imports `colorama` opportunistically (lines 46-50) and changes behaviour when present (`colors_supported`), but no manifest declares it. The dev toolchain (pytest, pytest-cov, coveralls, mypy, prospector) exists only as unpinned `pip install` lines in `.travis.yml` and prose in shell scripts. Windows 10+ consoles process ANSI natively, so colorama is no longer needed there.

## Evidence

ssh-audit.py:47 `from colorama import init as colorama_init`; line 229 `return 'colorama' in sys.modules or os.name == 'posix'`. No setup.py, requirements file or pyproject.toml.

## Impact

Colour behaviour depends on whatever is installed in the environment, invisibly. The dev tools are unpinned and undocumented.

## Fix

Drop the colorama import to keep the project stdlib-only. Decide colour support from `sys.stdout.isatty()` and the `NO_COLOR` env var, which also stops escape codes landing in redirected output. Add pyproject.toml with `dependencies = []` and `requires-python = ">=3.14"`.

## Resolution
colorama import removed; colors_supported requires POSIX, stdout.isatty() and no NO_COLOR (test_colors_supported_only_on_a_terminal). pyproject.toml declares dependencies = [] and requires-python >= 3.14; dev tools pinned in .pre-commit-config.yaml.
title: Undeclared optional colorama dependency; no project metadata declares dependencies

body:
## Problem

`KexDB.ALGORITHMS` and `SSH.Security.CVE` stop at OpenSSH 7.3 / Dropbear 2016.74 / libssh 0.7.3. Current defaults are absent: `curve25519-sha256`, `<email>`, `mlkem768x25519-sha256`, `rsa-sha2-*-<email>`, `sk-*` keys. The tool also announces itself as `SSH-2.0-OpenSSH_7.3` (line 1145).

## Evidence

`grep -c 'sntrup761\|mlkem768\|curve25519-sha256\x27' ssh-audit.py` → 0. `output_algorithm` emits `('warn', 'unknown algorithm')` for any name not in the DB (line 1690). The newest CVE row is CVE-2016-3116.

## Impact

Against any current OpenSSH, the post-quantum and default kex algorithms are flagged `[warn] unknown algorithm`, and no CVE after 2016 is reported. The security verdict is stale in both directions.

## Fix

Refresh the algorithm DB and CVE tables from OpenSSH/Dropbear/libssh release notes, or port the maintained data from the active fork (jtesta/ssh-audit, MIT). This is data work separate from the tooling modernisation; track it as its own change.

Not applied in the 2026-09-17 fix run: the user approved all fixes, and the fix prompt itself said this data refresh stays open. Confirmed live the same day: auditing a local `OpenSSH_9.6p1` server reports `<email>`, `curve25519-sha256`, `ext-info-s` and `<email>` as `[warn] unknown algorithm`, and recommends `+ssh-rsa` (SHA-1 signatures, disabled by default since OpenSSH 8.8).

## Resolution
SSH2 KexDB replaced by jtesta/ssh-audit v3.9.0 (commit dbf8b696) ssh2_kexdb.py MASTER_DB, programmatically verified identical (373 algorithms). Recommendation rules follow upstream (no appends for unknown software, pseudo/cert/sk/unversioned algorithms; unversioned faulty algorithms removable), minus upstream's modulus 'chg' action (no host-key/GEX measurement here); remove-all fallback kept. Version-based CVE/security matching removed, as upstream did (jtesta/ssh-audit#240: inaccurate due to distro backports) per user decision. Client banner now OpenSSH_10.3. Cross-checked against upstream's own tool on a local OpenSSH_9.6p1: identical verdicts on all 29 comparable algorithms. Tests: test_recommendations.py (mutation-checked), updated test_ssh2. LICENSE and header carry Joe Testa's copyright line.
title: Algorithm and CVE databases frozen at 2016; modern servers are misreported

body:
## Problem

Some commit subjects hold multi-sentence bodies (lengths 286, 208 and 182 characters), and the repository declares no commit message convention. The 8 sampled messages match their diffs, so there is no type misstatement.

## Evidence

`git log --format=%s | awk '{print length}' | sort -n | tail -3` → 182, 208, 286. For example 66b9e07 "Implement new options (-4/--ipv4, -6/--ipv6, -p/--port <port>). By default both IPv4 and IPv6 is supported and ...".

## Impact

Truncated one-line logs hide intent. With no convention, changelog and version decisions for the modernised fork stay manual.

## Fix

Published history is not rewritten. For new work, keep subjects at 72 characters or fewer with the detail in the body; optionally adopt Conventional Commits and add a prek `commit-msg` hook to enforce it.

Not applied in the 2026-09-17 fix run: published history is not rewritten, and choosing a commit convention is the maintainer's decision.

## Resolution
Not a defect of this fork: the flagged commits are inherited upstream history (Andris Raugulis and contributors), which the maintainer will not rewrite. The fork continues with its own commit style for new work; no convention change requested.
title: Commit subjects carry full bodies; no commit convention declared

body:
## Problem

`output()` sizes the padding column with `ml(names) = max(len(i) for i in names)`. For SSH1, `names` is `pkm.supported_ciphers` / `pkm.supported_authentications`, which are empty lists whenever the server's SMSG_PUBLIC_KEY mask has no bit set in the known range. `max()` of an empty sequence raises `ValueError`, which nothing catches. The server controls both masks, so a hostile or merely broken SSH1 server turns the audit into a Python traceback — the exact failure class the hostile-server hardening (test/test_hostile_server.py docstring: "never a traceback") claims to have closed.

## Evidence

ssh-audit.py:2044-2049
```python
def ml(names: list[str]) -> int:
    return max(len(i) for i in names)


...
if pkm is not None:
    maxlen = max(ml(pkm.supported_ciphers), ml(pkm.supported_authentications), maxlen)
```
Reproduction (SMSG_PUBLIC_KEY with cipher mask 0, auth mask 4):
```
pkm.supported_ciphers -> []
sa.output(banner, [], pkm=pkm) -> ValueError: max() iterable argument is empty
```
SSH2 is not affected only because `ReadBuf.read_list` always returns at least `['']`.

## Impact

An SSH1 server advertising no (known) ciphers or no (known) auth methods — cipher bit 7+ only, or mask 0 — aborts the run with a traceback and no report. Batch consumers get no structured error.

## Fix

Give `max` a default: `return max((len(i) for i in names), default=0)`. Add a test in test/test_hostile_server.py (or test_ssh1.py via `_serve(..., cmask=0)`) that audits an SSH1 server with cipher mask 0 and asserts the run completes with no `(enc)` lines.

## Resolution
output().ml uses max(..., default=0); test_ssh1.test_no_known_cipher_bits_is_reported_not_crashed audits an SSH1 server with cipher mask 1<<7 and completes.
title: SSH1 server with an empty cipher or authentication mask crashes the audit with a traceback

## Problem

Without `-p`, `from_cmdline` splits the target on every ':' and takes the first piece as the host. Any IPv6 literal is therefore mangled into a different target: `2001:db8::1` becomes host `2001` (which `getaddrinfo` resolves as the IPv4 address 0.0.7.209), `fe80::1` becomes `fe80` (looked up in DNS, including search domains), `[::1]:22` becomes `[`, and `::1` is rejected as "host is empty". When the piece count is not exactly 2 the port suffix is dropped too. Additionally, any positional argument after the first (`ssh-audit.py host1 host2`) is discarded without a message. The README documents `-4`/`-6` IPv6 support but never says an IPv6 literal needs `-p`.

## Evidence

ssh-audit.py:159-164
```python
s = args[0].split(':')
host = s[0].strip()
if len(s) == 2:
    oport, port = s[1], parse_int(s[1])
else:
    oport, port = '22', 22
```
Reproduction via `AuditConf.from_cmdline`:
```
['2001:db8::1']      -> ('2001', 22)
['fe80::1']          -> ('fe80', 22)
['[::1]:22']         -> ('[', 22)
['2001:db8::1:2222'] -> ('2001', 22)
['::1']              -> exit 1, 'host is empty'
['host1', 'host2']   -> ('host1', 22)
socket.getaddrinfo('2001', 22) -> ('0.0.7.209', 22)
```

## Impact

A user auditing an IPv6 server by address either gets a confusing error or — when the first hextet resolves through DNS search domains — audits and reports on an unrelated host under the name they typed. Extra targets silently go unaudited.

## Fix

Parse the target explicitly: accept `[addr]:port` and `[addr]`; treat a value with more than one ':' and no brackets as a bare host (no port); keep `host:port` for exactly one ':'. Reject `len(args) > 1` via `usage_cb('only one host may be given')`. Add cases for each form above to `test_audit_conf_cmdline`, and document the bracket syntax in README.

## Resolution
AuditConf._split_target accepts host, host:port, bare IPv6 and [addr]:port; -p overrides the target port; more than one host is a usage error. Covered by test_cmdline_ipv6_targets and test_cmdline_rejects_more_than_one_host; README documents the forms.
title: IPv6 address targets are split on ':' and audit the wrong host; extra positional arguments are silently ignored

## Problem

`get_banner` first waits 0.7 s for the server to speak; if that single `recv` times out it returns immediately with no banner and never sends its own identification string. RFC 4253 §4.2 requires both sides to send an identification string but does not require the server to go first, and real servers delay it: sshd behind tcp-wrappers/inetd doing reverse DNS, overloaded hosts, high-latency links, and implementations that wait for the client. All of them are reported as "did not receive banner." even though the existing `BANNER_TIMEOUT = 15.0` deadline loop would have handled a late banner.

## Evidence

ssh-audit.py:1054-1060
```python
rto = self._sock.gettimeout()
self._sock.settimeout(0.7)
s, e = self.recv()
self._sock.settimeout(rto)
if s < 0:
    return self.__banner, self.__header
self.send(banner.encode() + b'\r\n')
```
Reproduction against a local TCP server:
```
server sends banner after 1.0 s   -> exit 1 '[exception] did not receive banner.' (elapsed 0.8 s)
server waits for client ident     -> exit 1 '[exception] did not receive banner.'
```
test/test_errors.py:77-82 (`test_banner_read_timeout`) asserts this behaviour ("nothing was sent").

## Impact

Reachable, working SSH servers are reported as broken; in batch scans they silently drop out of the results.

## Fix

Send the client identification immediately after connect (as the OpenSSH client does), then read lines until the banner, EOF, the pre-banner cap, or `BANNER_TIMEOUT` — the existing loop already does the last three. Delete the 0.7 s probe. Update `test_banner_read_timeout` to assert the identification *was* sent and add a test where the banner arrives only after the client's identification.

## Resolution
get_banner sends the client identification first and relies on BANNER_TIMEOUT; the 0.7 s probe is gone. Real-socket repro: banner after 1.0 s and server-waits-for-client both audit successfully (exit 0). test_client_identification_is_sent_before_reading added.
title: Banner exchange gives up after 0.7 s of server silence without ever sending the client identification

## Problem

The banner read has a 15 s wall-clock deadline because "the deadline stops a tarpit that trickles lines just inside the read timeout" (comment at ssh-audit.py:988-989). The packet reader has no equivalent: `ensure_read` and `_drain` loop on `recv` until enough bytes arrive, and the only bound is the 5 s per-`recv` socket timeout. A server that sends one byte every <5 s keeps `read_packet` alive for up to `packet_length` × 5 s — 256 KiB × 5 s ≈ 15 days for an SSH2 packet at `MAX_PACKET_LENGTH`.

## Evidence

ssh-audit.py:1116-1120
```python
def ensure_read(self, size: int) -> None:
    while self.unread_len < size:
        s, e = self.recv()
        if s < 0:
            raise SSH.Socket.InsufficientReadException(e)
```
`_drain` (1182-1187) has the same shape. Reproduction: local server sends a valid banner, then `packet_length=1020, padding=4`, then one byte every 3 s:
```
trickle: still reading after 40 s (BANNER_TIMEOUT is 15 s, per-recv timeout 5 s)
```

## Impact

One tarpit host (endlessh-style, or a hostile server) stalls a single audit for hours to days; in a scripted sweep over many hosts it blocks every host behind it.

## Fix

Give `read_packet` a wall-clock deadline (e.g. `PACKET_TIMEOUT = 15.0`, set with `time.monotonic()` at entry) and check it in `ensure_read` and `_drain`, raising `InsufficientReadException('timeout')` when exceeded. Add a test in test_hostile_server.py that patches `time.monotonic` (as `test_slow_pre_banner_lines_hit_deadline` does) and asserts a trickled packet ends in `error reading packet (timeout)`.

## Resolution
read_packet sets a PACKET_TIMEOUT (15 s) deadline checked by ensure_read and _drain. Real-socket trickle repro now ends at 15.1 s with '[exception] error reading packet (timeout)'. Tests: test_trickled_packet_hits_deadline, test_trickled_oversized_packet_drain_hits_deadline.
title: Packet reads have no overall deadline; a trickling server holds the audit open indefinitely

## Problem

The algorithm DB format is `[versions, fail texts, warn texts, info texts]`. Both XMSS entries place `WARN_EXPERIMENTAL` in index 1, the failure slot. The tool therefore prints `[fail] using experimental algorithm` and scores the algorithm as a failure (10 points per fail) in recommendations, so removal is shown with `out.fail`. The defect is inherited verbatim from jtesta/ssh-audit v3.9.0 (ssh2_kexdb.py lines 287-288), but the port comment's "verbatim" does not make the output right.

## Evidence

ssh-audit.py:1469-1470
```python
'<email>': [['7.7'], [WARN_EXPERIMENTAL]],
'<email>': [['7.7'], [WARN_EXPERIMENTAL]],
```
A scan of every DB entry for texts whose constant prefix does not match its slot (FAIL_ in 1, WARN_ in 2, INFO_ in 3) returns exactly these two:
```
[('key', '<email>', 1, 'WARN_EXPERIMENTAL'), ('key', '<email>', 1, 'WARN_EXPERIMENTAL')]
```

## Impact

Servers offering XMSS get a failure line and a fail-level removal recommendation for what the database itself classifies as a warning.

## Fix

Change both entries to `[['7.7'], [], [WARN_EXPERIMENTAL]]` and note the deviation from upstream in the port comment. Add a test that asserts every text in slot 1/2/3 is a FAIL_/WARN_/INFO_ constant respectively (the scan above), so a future re-port cannot reintroduce it.

## Resolution
Both XMSS entries now [['7.7'], [], [WARN_EXPERIMENTAL]]; deviation from upstream noted in the KexDB port comment. test_every_database_note_sits_in_its_level_slot guards every slot.
title: XMSS host-key entries put a warning in the failure slot and are reported as [fail]

## Problem

`ReadBuf.read_mpint2`, `ReadBuf.read_string` (only caller: `read_mpint2`) and `WriteBuf.write_mpint2` (with the signed branch of `_create_mpint`) have no caller in ssh-audit.py; only test_buffer.py exercises them. The earlier unwired-code fix removed the DH key-exchange classes that used them and left these behind. `read_mpint2` is also wrong: it unpacks every 4-byte word with signed `'>i'` when the value is negative, so any later word with its top bit set is OR-ed in as a negative number and wipes the high words. The existing tests only cover negatives of one word or with non-negative later words, so the bug does not show.

## Evidence

ssh-audit.py:649-655
```python
pad, sf = (b'\xff', '>i') if ord(v[0:1]) & 0x80 else (b'\x00', '>I')
return self._parse_mpint(v, pad, sf)
```
AST reference scan of ssh-audit.py: `read_mpint2`, `write_mpint2` defined but never referenced; `read_string` referenced only at 651. Round-trip reproduction:
```
n = -9223372032559808513  encoded 80000000ffffffff  read_mpint2 -> -1
n = -549755814143         encoded ff7fffffff01      read_mpint2 -> -255
```

## Impact

Dead code with a latent bug, kept at 100% coverage only by its own tests; anyone wiring SSH2 key parsing back in inherits a broken decoder.

## Fix

Delete `read_mpint2`, `read_string`, `write_mpint2`, the `signed` parameter/branch of `_create_mpint`, and `test_mpint2` in test/test_buffer.py. If kept instead, decode with `int.from_bytes(v, 'big', signed=True)` and add the two cases above to `test_mpint2`.

## Resolution
Deleted read_mpint2, read_string, write_mpint2, _parse_mpint and the signed branch; _create_mpint is int.to_bytes and read_mpint1 is int.from_bytes. test_mpint2 removed; test_mpint1 gains top-bit and multi-word cases.
title: Unwired SSH2 mpint codec: read_mpint2/write_mpint2/read_string are test-only, and read_mpint2 decodes multi-word negatives wrongly

## Problem

`Colors.enabled` turns colour off whenever the `NO_COLOR` key exists. The no-color.org convention, which the `Colors` docstring links as its authority, says colour is disabled only when `NO_COLOR` is "present and not an empty string". `NO_COLOR=` (commonly left behind by `export NO_COLOR=` or env templating) wrongly disables colour.

## Evidence

ssh-audit.py:2181
```python
return os.name == 'posix' and 'NO_COLOR' not in os.environ and bool(isatty and isatty())
```
Reproduction: `os.environ['NO_COLOR'] = ''` with a tty stream → `Colors.enabled(...)` returns `False`.

## Impact

Behaviour differs from the documented standard and from other NO_COLOR-aware tools.

## Fix

Use `not os.environ.get('NO_COLOR')`. Extend `test_colors_supported_only_on_a_terminal` with `{'NO_COLOR': ''}` expecting `True`.

Colors.enabled uses `not os.environ.get('NO_COLOR')`; test_colors_supported_only_on_a_terminal asserts NO_COLOR='' keeps colour.

body:
## Problem

`usage()` always ends with `sys.exit(1)`, so an explicit `-h`/`--help` request reports failure; README says status 1 means an error. The usage synopsis `[-1246pbnvl]` leaves out `h`, although `-h` is listed below it. `usage()` also builds a fresh `Output()` whose `colors` is always `True`, so a command-line error on a terminal is printed in colour even when `-n` was given (`-n -p x host`).

## Evidence

ssh-audit.py:33-51
```python
def usage(err: str | None = None) -> NoReturn:
    uout = Output()
    ...
    uout.info(f'usage: {p} [-1246pbnvl] <host>\n')
    ...
    sys.exit(1)
```
`./ssh-audit.py --help` → return code 1 (15 lines on stdout). README.md:41: "errors are written to stderr and exit with status 1."

## Impact

Scripts and wrappers that treat a non-zero exit as failure misreport `--help`; `-n` is not honoured for the one class of output printed before option parsing ends.

## Fix

`sys.exit(1 if err is not None else 0)` — keeping status 1 for the no-host case by passing it an error such as `usage_cb('host is required')`; change the synopsis to `[-h1246pbnvl]` in both usage() and README; set `uout.colors = '-n' not in sys.argv and '--no-colors' not in sys.argv` or have from_cmdline pass the parsed colour flag to `usage_cb`. Update `test_no_arguments_prints_usage_and_exits_1` and add a `--help` exit-0 test in test_main.py.

## Resolution
usage exits 0 without an error, 1 with one (no host now reports 'host is required'); synopsis is [-h1246pbnvl] in code and README; from_cmdline passes the -n state to usage_cb. Tests: test_cmdline_help_exits_0_and_errors_exit_1, test_cmdline_errors_honour_no_colors, test_main.test_help_exits_0.
title: --help exits with status 1, the usage line omits -h, and argument errors ignore -n

## Problem

The test asserts that after the first 0.7 s read times out the client has sent nothing ("the server never spoke first"). That is the behaviour that makes servers which delay their banner or wait for the client unauditable (see the banner-exchange reliability finding). The test is therefore a regression guard for a defect: the correct fix will fail it, and the suite has no test with a banner that arrives after the client's identification.

## Evidence

test/test_errors.py:77-82
```python
def test_banner_read_timeout(self):
    self.vsocket.rdata.append(TimeoutError('timed out'))
    lines = self._audit_fails()
    self.assertEqual(lines, ['[exception] did not receive banner.'])
    # nothing was sent: the server never spoke first
    self.assertEqual(self.vsocket.sdata, [])
```

## Impact

The suite passes at 100% coverage while guaranteeing the wrong protocol behaviour.

## Fix

When fixing the banner exchange, change the last assertion to `self.assertEqual(len(self.vsocket.sdata), 1)` (identification sent) and add a test whose rdata is `[TimeoutError(...), b'SSH-2.0-OpenSSH_9.9\r\n', <kexinit packet>]` that completes an audit.

## Resolution
test_banner_read_timeout now asserts the identification was sent and the '(timeout)' reason.
title: test_banner_read_timeout locks in the defective no-send banner behaviour

## Problem

`get_banner` stops on read timeout, connection reset, EOF, the 1024-line pre-banner cap, or the 15 s deadline, then returns only `(None, header)`. `audit()` turns every case into the same `[exception] did not receive banner.`; the `e` reason from `recv` is discarded. A user cannot tell a firewall timeout from a reset from a tarpit that hit the cap.

## Evidence

ssh-audit.py:1056-1059, 1067-1070 (`s, e = self.recv()` — `e` never used), 1084-1085 (cap/deadline `break` with no reason) and 2121-2122:
```python
if banner is None:
    err = '[exception] did not receive banner.'
```
test_errors.py `test_banner_read_timeout`, `test_connection_closed_before_banner` and test_hostile_server.py `test_endless_pre_banner_lines_stop` / `test_slow_pre_banner_lines_hit_deadline` all assert the identical message for different causes.

## Impact

Failed audits are hard to diagnose; the tool's only error signal carries no cause.

Record the stop reason in `get_banner` (the `recv` error string, 'connection closed', 'too many pre-banner lines', 'banner timeout') and report `[exception] did not receive banner ({reason}).` Update the four tests to assert their specific reason.

get_banner returns a stop reason (recv error text, 'connection closed', 'timeout', 'too many pre-banner lines'); audit prints 'did not receive banner (<reason>).' Each cause is asserted in test_errors/test_hostile_server.
title: "did not receive banner" hides which of five causes ended the banner read

## Problem

`_resolve` catches only `OSError` around `socket.getaddrinfo`. For a host name with a label longer than 63 characters (or an empty label, or other IDNA-invalid input) `getaddrinfo` raises `UnicodeError`, which is not an `OSError`, so it escapes as an uncaught traceback instead of the tool's `[exception] ...` error line.

## Evidence

ssh-audit.py:1018-1028
```python
try:
    ...
    r = socket.getaddrinfo(self.__host, self.__port, family, stype)
    ...
except OSError as e:
    out.error(f'[exception] {e}')
    sys.exit(1)
```
Reproduction:
```
socket.getaddrinfo('a'*64 + '.example', 22) -> UnicodeEncodeError (isinstance OSError: False)
./ssh-audit.py aaaa…(64).example -> exit 1, traceback ending "encoding with 'idna' codec failed"
```

A mistyped or over-long host name prints a Python traceback on stderr instead of a one-line error; scripts parsing stderr for `[exception]` miss it.

_resolve catches (OSError, UnicodeError); a 64-char label now prints one [exception] line. test_idna_invalid_host_name added.

## Problem

`output_recommendations` pads each name with `' ' * (padlen - len(name))`, where `padlen` is one more than the longest algorithm the server offers. Names to *append* come from the database, not from the server, so they can be longer; the padding count goes negative, produces an empty string, and the name runs straight into `--`, breaking column alignment and the `name -- text` shape that batch consumers split on.

## Evidence

ssh-audit.py (output_recommendations)
```python
p = '' if out.batch else ' ' * (padlen - len(name))
...
fm = '(rec) {0}{1}{2}-- {3} algorithm to {4} {5}'
```
Observed while regenerating the README example (non-batch, OpenSSH 9.6 banner, kex list whose longest offered name is `diffie-hellman-group14-sha256`):
```
(rec) -diffie-hellman-group14-sha256 -- kex algorithm to remove
(rec) +<email>-- kex algorithm to append
```

## Impact

Misaligned report and a line whose separator lacks its leading space.

## Fix

Include the recommended names in the width: compute `padlen` in `output_recommendations` as `max(padlen, max(len(n) for n in every rec name) + 1)` before printing, or pad with `max(padlen - len(name), 1)`. Add a test auditing an OpenSSH 9.x server whose offered kex names are all shorter than a recommended append, asserting ` -- ` follows the name.

## Resolution
padlen widened to longest recommended name; covered by test_recommended_names_longer_than_offered_ones_stay_aligned
title: Recommendation lines for appended names longer than every offered name lose the space before "--"

## Problem

`SSH.Software.parse` matches libssh only as `^libssh-([\d\.]+\d+)(.*)`. libssh's own default identification string uses an underscore, so every current libssh server is parsed as unknown software. The libssh version data in `KexDB` (`l10.6.0`, …) is then unreachable for real servers: no `(gen) software:` line, and `get_alg_recommendations` suppresses all "append" advice because `known is None`. The tests encode the same wrong format (`test_software.py:92-97`, `test_version_compare.py:20` build `SSH-2.0-libssh-<v>`), so the suite passes against a banner libssh does not emit.

## Evidence

ssh-audit.py:933
```python
mx = re.match(r'^libssh-([\d\.]+\d+)(.*)', software)
```
libssh source, include/libssh/priv.h:223 (libssh-mirror, fetched this run):
```c
#define CLIENT_BANNER_SSH2 "SSH-2.0-libssh_" SSH_STRINGIFY(LIBSSH_VERSION)
```
Measured:
```
SSH-2.0-libssh_0.9.6  -> None
SSH-2.0-libssh_0.11.1 -> None
SSH-2.0-libssh-0.6.0  -> <Software(product=libssh, version=0.6.0)>
```

## Impact

README advertises libssh history and recommendations ("historical information from OpenSSH, Dropbear SSH and libssh"). For every libssh server in the field the audit prints no software line and no append recommendations, so the libssh half of that feature is dead.

## Fix

Accept both separators: `re.match(r'^libssh[-_]([\d\.]+\d+)(.*)', software)`. Add `SSH-2.0-libssh_0.9.6` and `SSH-2.0-libssh_0.11.1` cases to `test_libssh_software`, and switch `get_libssh_software` in test_version_compare.py to the underscore form (keep one hyphen case for pre-0.7 servers).

## Resolution
Software.parse now matches `^libssh[-_]`, so both the modern underscore form and pre-0.7 hyphen form parse. Verified: SSH-2.0-libssh_0.9.6 and _0.11.1 now yield libssh software objects. test_software gained both underscore cases; test_version_compare's libssh fixtures switched to the underscore banner.
title: libssh servers are not recognised: the parser expects "libssh-", libssh announces "libssh_"

## Problem

`Colors.enabled` returns False whenever `os.name != 'posix'` (by design: Windows gets plain text). Three tests fake a TTY and assert ANSI codes without pinning `os.name`, so they fail on Windows. CI runs `python -W error -m unittest discover -s test -v` on `[ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest]`; the Windows job will be red on the first push of this branch.

## Evidence

ssh-audit.py:2331
```python
return os.name == 'posix' and not os.environ.get('NO_COLOR') and bool(isatty and isatty())
```
Reproduced by running the full suite with the module's `os` replaced by a namespace whose `name` is `'nt'`:
```
Ran 133 tests
FAILED (failures=3)
FAILED: test_colors.TestColors.test_buffered_algorithm_lines_are_colored_by_level
FAILED: test_colors.TestColors.test_errors_are_red_on_a_terminal_stderr
FAILED: test_output.TestOutput.test_colors_supported_only_on_a_terminal
```
.github/workflows/ci.yml:53 `os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest]`

## Impact

The test matrix never goes green, which trains contributors to ignore a failing required check; the Windows-specific "no colour" behaviour itself is untested.

## Fix

Pin the platform in those tests: in `TestColors.setUp` and in `test_colors_supported_only_on_a_terminal`, add `mock.patch.object(self.sa.os, 'name', 'posix')` (start + addCleanup). Add one test asserting `Colors.enabled(tty)` is False with `os.name` patched to `'nt'`, so the Windows branch is exercised on every OS.

## Resolution
The two colour-asserting tests now stub Colors.enabled through a `colors_on(stream)` helper that answers True only for the expected stream, preserving the buffered-stream regression they guard. test_colors_supported_only_on_a_terminal derives its expectation from `os.name == 'posix'`. New test_colors_disabled_off_posix patches os.name to 'nt' around a single Colors.enabled call. Deliberately NOT patching os.name suite-wide: it also drives pathlib, and doing so broke all 136 tests in simulation. Verified with a harness that swaps the `os` seen by the script and test modules for one reporting 'nt': 136 tests pass.
title: Three colour tests assume POSIX and fail on the windows-latest CI leg

body:
## Problem

`output()` prints the whole pre-banner header as one call: `out.info('(gen) header: ' + '\n'.join(header))`. Only the first line carries the `(gen) header:` prefix; every later line is server-chosen text starting at column 0. Control characters are escaped, but plain text such as `(kex) mlkem768x25519-sha256 -- [info] ...` is indistinguishable from a real algorithm line, in batch output as well.

## Evidence

Hostile server sends two header lines, then an OpenSSH 9.6 banner and a KEXINIT offering only ecdh-sha2-nistp256/ssh-rsa/aes128-cbc/hmac-sha1. Batch output (`-b`):
```
(gen) header: (gen) software: OpenSSH 10.3
(kex) mlkem768x25519-sha256 -- [info] available since OpenSSH 9.9
(gen) banner: SSH-2.0-OpenSSH_9.6
(gen) software: OpenSSH 9.6
```
The second line is forged; the server never offered that kex.

## Impact

An audited server can inject arbitrary report lines, such as fake post-quantum kex entries or fake `(gen)` lines, into output that people and batch parsers treat as the auditor's findings. It cannot remove real `[fail]` lines, hence Low.

## Fix

Print one prefixed line per header line: `for line in header: out.info('(gen) header: ' + line)`. Add a test to test_hostile_server.py asserting that every stdout line from a two-line header starts with `(gen) header: `.

## Resolution
output() now prints one `(gen) header: ` line per header line instead of joining them with newlines. Output.escape's docstring updated, since the newline rationale it cited no longer applies. New test_every_header_line_is_prefixed asserts a forged `(kex) ...` second line is prefixed and never appears bare.
title: Server pre-banner lines after the first print unprefixed and forge audit report lines

body:
## Problem

Nothing handles `BrokenPipeError` when stdout's reader exits (`| head`, `| grep -m1`, a pager quit). The audit already completed, but the process prints a Python traceback to stderr and exits 1, which the README defines as "error".

## Evidence

Against a local one-shot SSH2 server:
```
$ python3 ssh-audit.py -n -p $P 127.0.0.1 2>err | head -1; echo ${PIPESTATUS[0]}
# general
1
$ tail err
  File ".../ssh-audit.py", line 324, in <lambda>
    return lambda x: print(self.escape(x))
BrokenPipeError: [Errno 32] Broken pipe
```
The same run with stdout to /dev/null exits 0.

## Impact

Shell pipelines see a spurious failure status, and the tool's own "errors go to stderr as one `[exception]` line" contract is broken by a traceback.

## Fix

In the `__main__` block, wrap `audit(conf)`: on `BrokenPipeError`, point stdout at devnull (`os.dup2(os.open(os.devnull, os.O_WRONLY), sys.stdout.fileno())`, as the Python docs' signal-handling note prescribes, so the interpreter's final flush does not raise again) and `sys.exit(141)`, or 0 if you prefer `head` semantics. Test with test_main.py by replacing stdout with a stream whose `write` raises `BrokenPipeError` and asserting a clean exit with nothing on stderr.

## Resolution
__main__ catches BrokenPipeError, replaces sys.stdout with a StringIO so the interpreter's final flush cannot raise, and exits 141 (128 + SIGPIPE). StringIO rather than an open devnull file: the first attempt leaked a descriptor and surfaced as a ResourceWarning that failed the suite under -W error. Verified against a local server: `| head -1` prints the first line, exits 141, with empty stderr even under python3 -W error.
title: Piping the report into a reader that closes early ends in a BrokenPipeError traceback and exit 1

body:
## Problem

`usage(err)` prints the error through `uout.error` (stderr) but prints the header and every usage line through `uout.head`/`uout.info` (stdout), even when exiting 1. This is the same defect class already fixed for audit errors: `Output.error`'s docstring says errors on stdout "were written into redirected reports" and "batch consumers parsed them as audit lines".

## Evidence

ssh-audit.py:40-58
```python
uout = Output()
...
uout.head(f'# {p} {VERSION}, https://github.com/ivuorinen/ssh-audit\n')
if err is not None:
    uout.error(err)
uout.info(f'usage: {p} [-h1246pbnvl] <host>\n')
...
sys.exit(0 if err is None else 1)
```
`ssh-audit.py -b -l bogus host > report.txt` writes 12 usage lines into report.txt and exits 1.

## Impact

Redirected reports and batch parsers receive help text on failure; README line 42 ("errors are written to stderr") is only half true.

## Fix

When `err is not None`, route the usage text to stderr as well: e.g. wrap the body in `contextlib.redirect_stdout(sys.stderr)` when `err` is set. Keep `-h` output on stdout. Extend test_cmdline_help_exits_0_and_errors_exit_1 to assert that `output['out']` is empty for the error cases.

## Resolution
usage() wraps its body in contextlib.redirect_stdout(sys.stderr) when err is set, so a command-line failure puts the whole message on stderr. Verified: `-l bogus host` writes 0 lines to stdout and the header plus error to stderr; `-h` still writes to stdout with empty stderr and exit 0. test_cmdline_help_exits_0_and_errors_exit_1 now asserts which stream each case uses; test_cmdline_rejects_more_than_one_host updated, as it had assumed the error was the first stderr line.
title: On a command-line error the usage text is written to stdout, only the error line to stderr

body:
## Problem

The workflow pins all four actions to full commit SHAs (all four verified against their tags this run). The lint job then runs `prek run --all-files`, which clones `astral-sh/ruff-pre-commit` at `rev: v0.16.8` and `pre-commit/mirrors-mypy` at `rev: v2.3.1`. Those are git tags and can be moved, so the SHA pinning is bypassed for the code the lint job actually executes.

## Evidence

.pre-commit-config.yaml:19-29
```yaml
  - repo: https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff-pre-commit
    rev: v0.16.8
  - repo: https://github.com/pre-commit/mirrors-mypy
    rev: v2.3.1
```
.github/workflows/ci.yml:28-31 runs `j178/prek-action` with `extra-args: --all-files --skip unittest`.

## Impact

A retagged hook repository runs attacker-chosen code in CI with the job's token (contents: read) and checkout. The blast radius is small because permissions are read-only and credentials are not persisted, hence Low.

## Fix

Freeze both revs to commit SHAs with the tag as a comment (`prek autoupdate --freeze` or `pre-commit autoupdate --freeze`), e.g. `rev: <sha>  # frozen: v0.16.8`, matching the workflow's `# v7.0.1` style.

## Resolution
Both hook repos pinned to commit SHAs with `# frozen: <tag>` comments (ruff-pre-commit 2eeb5678de71a00c0902cbda7105d328432f72cb, mirrors-mypy 7ff8d35ae36a7d2b968f2f90b4c723e292e594ee), each resolved from its tag via the GitHub API this run. Verified with `prek run --all-files --skip unittest`: every hook resolved and passed.
title: CI lint job executes hook repos pinned by mutable tags while every action is SHA-pinned

body:
## Problem

The usage notes state colours are used "only when stdout is a terminal". The implementation adds two conditions the README omits: colour is never used on Windows (`os.name == 'posix'`), and error lines are coloured when stderr, not stdout, is a terminal. The changelog line 125 mentions "POSIX terminals", but the usage section, which is what users read, does not.

## Evidence

README.md:43
```
* colors are used only when stdout is a terminal; set a non-empty `NO_COLOR` or pass `-n` to disable them.
```
ssh-audit.py:2331 `return os.name == 'posix' and ...`; ssh-audit.py:263 `if self.colors and Colors.enabled(sys.stderr):`

## Impact

Windows users following the README expect colour and get none; the stderr rule is undocumented.

## Fix

Reword: "colors are used only on POSIX terminals: report lines when stdout is a terminal, errors when stderr is; set a non-empty `NO_COLOR` or pass `-n` to disable them."

## Resolution
README usage notes now state colour is POSIX-only, report lines follow stdout and errors follow stderr, and that a command-line error writes usage to stderr. Changelog gained entries for the four behaviour changes in this pass.
title: README says colours follow "stdout is a terminal"; they are POSIX-only and errors colour by stderr

body:
## Problem

`_fix_date(d: str)` guards `d is not None`, and it does receive None: the NetBSD pattern's date group is optional, so `mx.group(1)` is None for banners like `OpenSSH_4.4 NetBSD`. mypy strict passes only because `re.Match.group` returns `str | Any`, and the `Any` swallows the mismatch. This is an unchecked-declaration: the signature lies, and the None guard reads as dead code to a reader who trusts it.

## Evidence

ssh-audit.py:888-900
```python
def _fix_date(d: str) -> str | None:
    if d is not None and len(d) == 8:
...
mx = re.match(r'^NetBSD(?:_Secure_Shell)?(?:[\s-]+(\d{8})(.*))?$', c)
if mx:
    d = cls._fix_date(mx.group(1))
```
test_software.py:129 exercises it: `'SSH-2.0-OpenSSH_4.4 NetBSD'` → `'NetBSD'`.

## Impact

A refactor that trusts the annotation and drops the guard crashes with `TypeError: object of type 'NoneType' has no len()` on every date-less NetBSD banner, and the type checker will not flag it.

## Fix

Annotate `d: str | None` and add a one-line docstring naming why None arrives (the optional NetBSD date group).

## Resolution
_fix_date is annotated `d: str | None` and carries a docstring naming where None comes from (the optional NetBSD date group).
title: _fix_date is declared to take str but is called with None; mypy strict cannot see it

body:
## Problem

The five report levels (`info`, `good`, `warn`, `fail`, `head`) are served by a catch-all `__getattr__` typed `Callable[[str], None]`. Any attribute name type-checks under mypy strict, and `getlevel` ranks unknown names above `fail`, so a typo like `out.wran(...)` compiles, bypasses `-l`, and prints without colour. This is an any-escape covering every output call in the program, and dynamic dispatch where five plain methods would do.

## Evidence

ssh-audit.py:235-240, 317-324
```python
if cname not in self.LEVELS:
    return sys.maxsize
...
def __getattr__(self, name: str) -> Callable[[str], None]:
    ...
    if not self.getlevel(name) >= self.__minlevel:
```
Only five names are used anywhere: `out.fail/good/head/info/warn` plus `getattr(out, level)` at 2041 with level from `['fail','warn','info']`.

## Impact

An output typo becomes a silent behaviour change (ignores `-l fail`, loses colour) that neither ruff nor mypy nor a passing test run reports.

## Fix

Replace `__getattr__` with one private `_emit(level, text)` plus five one-line methods (`def warn(self, text: str) -> None: self._emit('warn', text)`, …). Replace `getattr(out, level)` at 2041 with a dict lookup or `_emit(level, …)`. mypy then rejects unknown names.

## Resolution
__getattr__ replaced by a private _emit(level, text) plus explicit head/good/info/warn/fail methods; output_algorithm dispatches through a `printers` dict instead of getattr(out, level). A misspelled level is now a mypy error. Coverage stayed at 100% of statements and branches.
title: Output.__getattr__ turns every misspelled level into a valid, always-printed, uncoloured call

body:
## Problem

Three leftovers from the removed Python 2 and upstream code. (1) `class Socket(ReadBuf, WriteBuf)`: Socket sends with `self._sock.send` and never calls a WriteBuf method; `read_packet` builds its own `header = WriteBuf()`. The base only adds an unused `_wbuf` BytesIO and a cooperative-`super()` chain that ReadBuf's `__init__` exists to feed. (2) `alg_name_native = alg_name` at 1841 and 2022 is an identity alias (formerly a py2 unicode conversion). (3) `assert len(skey) == 3` / `assert len(hkey) == 3` restate what `tuple[int, int, int]` already declares; bandit flags both (B101).

## Evidence

Usage scan of ssh-audit.py: inside `class Socket` (1039-1310) there is no `self.write*` call; `alg_name_native` appears only at 1841/1842 and 2022-2024 as a rename of `alg_name`; bandit reports B101 at 552 and 553.

## Impact

A reader has to prove each of these is inert. The unused base makes Socket look like a two-way buffer it is not.

## Fix

`class Socket(ReadBuf):` (keep `super().__init__()` in ReadBuf or drop it with the MRO no longer shared); use `alg_name` directly at both sites; delete the two asserts. Run `make check`; coverage stays at 100% because only dead lines leave.

## Resolution
Socket now inherits ReadBuf only; both alg_name_native aliases use alg_name directly; the two tuple-length asserts are gone. bandit reports no issues on ssh-audit.py (was 2 x B101).
title: Dead structure: SSH.Socket inherits WriteBuf but never writes; alg_name_native aliases; redundant tuple-length asserts

body:
## Problem

The auditor never sends a KEXINIT or SMSG_PUBLIC_KEY; its docstrings say so ("the auditor never sends a KEXINIT, the tests build them"). The shipped single-file tool still carries `SSH2.Kex.write`/`.payload`, `SSH1.PublicKeyMessage.write`/`.payload`, and the WriteBuf methods only they call: `write_bool`, `write_list`, `write_string` and `write_mpint1`. The previous round removed `write_mpint2`/`read_string` for exactly this reason ("test-only").

## Evidence

Call-site scan of ssh-audit.py: `write_bool` only at 458, `write_list` only at 448-457, `write_string` only at 733 (inside write_list), `write_mpint1` only at 628-632; all inside `Kex.write`/`PublicKeyMessage.write`, which have no production caller. `.payload` has no production reference.

## Impact

About 60 lines of the audited, 100%-coverage-gated product exist only as test fixtures; coverage counts them as covered, so they inflate confidence in the shipped path.

## Fix

Move the builders to test/helpers.py as plain functions (`kexinit_payload(kex)`, `pkm_payload(pkm)`, with a local writer) and delete the four `write`/`payload` members and the four WriteBuf methods from ssh-audit.py. Keep `write`, `write_byte`, `write_int`, `write_flush` and `_create_mpint`, which read_packet and the fingerprint use.

## Resolution
Kex.write/.payload, PublicKeyMessage.write/.payload and WriteBuf.write_bool/write_string/write_list/write_mpint1 removed from the script; equivalent helpers (write_bool, write_string, write_list, write_mpint1, serialize_kex, serialize_pkm) now live in test/helpers.py and are used by test_ssh1, test_ssh2 and test_buffer. WriteBuf's docstring states what remains and why. ssh-audit.py's covered statements dropped from 1296 to 1262, still 100%.
title: Unwired: KEXINIT/SMSG_PUBLIC_KEY serialisers ship in the tool but only tests reach them

body:
## Problem

For repeated `SSH-x.y-` prefixes, the docstring promises "the lowest protocol version kept", but `min()` runs over tuples of digit strings, so minor versions of different lengths order lexicographically. This is the same defect class as the fixed version-comparison finding, on a path no real server currently exercises.

## Evidence

ssh-audit.py:1017-1018
```python
protocol = min(re.findall(cls.RX_PROTOCOL, mx.group(1)))
protocol = (int(protocol[0]), int(protocol[1]))
```
Measured: `SSH-1.5-SSH-1.10-x` → `(1, 10)`; the lowest is `(1, 5)`.

## Impact

Only the displayed minor version can be wrong, and only for a banner with two same-major prefixes of different minor-digit counts; the SSH1 detection (`protocol[0] == 1`) is unaffected.

## Fix

`protocol = min((int(a), int(b)) for a, b in re.findall(cls.RX_PROTOCOL, mx.group(1)))`, replacing both lines; add the `SSH-1.5-SSH-1.10-x` case to test_banners_with_multiple_protocols.

## Resolution
Banner.parse builds integer pairs before min(), so repeated prefixes compare numerically. Verified: SSH-1.5-SSH-1.10-x now yields (1, 5); the case is asserted in test_banners_with_multiple_protocols.
title: Banner.parse picks the lowest repeated protocol version by string comparison
